transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-25 15:00 PT
Duration: 45 min
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Samira Khan (Orion CTO), Diego Ruiz (Orion Lead SWE), Priya Nair (Orion Security), Tom Becker (Orion DevOps)
Meeting ID: ff-20270625-orion-001

Auto-generated summary: quick SDK walkthrough, auth and env setup. Action items at end.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep this to 45 minutes. quick agenda - show the Python and TypeScript quickstarts, auth options, environment setup, and then talk about the pilot and benchmarks. Arjun is going to drive the demo.
[00:18] Samira: thanks Maya, excited to see the SDK flow. we're trying to move from prototyping to a more controlled infra, want to understand how Redwood handles auth and private data - pii specifically.
[00:30] Arjun: great. quick note on attendees, and i'll do a live run of the python quickstart from a sample repo. bear with me if the screen share lags.
[00:45] Arjun: ok first, installing the SDK. pip install redwood-sdk, or npm i @redwood/inference for TS. typical install, you can see the README at https://docs.redwood-inference.com/sdk-quickstart - i'll paste links after the call.
[01:10] Diego: is there a single unified package for embeddings and chat? or different clients?
[01:22] Arjun: unified client. in python it's basically from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')). For TS: import {RedwoodClient} from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
[01:47] Priya: when you say api_key in env, what are best practices? we want rotation and auditability.
[01:55] Lena: yeah best practice is use short lived service keys for apps and rotate with your secret manager. for pilots you can start with standard api keys. for enterprise we support service accounts and integration with KMS/HSM and you can use SAML-backed SSO for the control plane.
[02:22] Tom: can you expand on service accounts? how do they look in the SDK?
[02:30] Arjun: service accounts are just an identity tied to a customer-managed workload. you'll exchange a certificate or token from your OIDC provider for a short-lived token that you feed to the SDK. pseudocode: token = exchange_oidc(); client = RedwoodClient(token=token) - apologies that's a simplified version. For a step-by-step we'll share the service-account doc.
[02:55] Samira: ok and for Private or VPC deployments, does auth change?
[03:02] Maya: not really - control plane auth uses SSO and RBAC; data plane in Private is within your VPC so you can use your internal identity provider and KMS. there are minor differences in how keys are distributed but the SDK usage is effectively identical.
[03:30] Arjun: moving on - environment setup. we recommend a 3-env approach: dev/staging/prod. set REDWOOD_ENV and REDWOOD_API_KEY in your CI secrets or runtime environment. example .env: REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx, REDWOOD_ENV=prod, REDWOOD_REGION=us-west-2.
[03:56] Diego: do you support multiple api keys per app? we want to separate ingest service from user-facing components.
[04:02] Arjun: yes you can create multiple keys with scoped permissions - you can also scope by model route. we'll show the console in a sec.
[04:18] [04:30] Screen share - Arjun shows Redwood Console: routes, keys, and quickstart repo.
[04:45] Arjun: here is the SDK quickstart repo - github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (note: transcription may mangle repo path).
[05:05] Samira: can you show the python chat example?
[05:12] Arjun: sure. code snippet readout: 
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
  resp = client.chat.create(model='redwood-7b', input='Summarize patient intake notes')
  print(resp.output)
[05:40] Diego: slight aside - you mentioned redwood-7b. do you have recommended models for latency vs quality?
[05:48] Arjun: yes, we maintain a model catalog. for lower latency use quantized variants or smaller families, for high quality use larger models. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles and batching rules per route.
[06:15] Priya: audit logs - where are calls logged and how long retained? we have strict retention and audit needs.
[06:24] Maya: hosted API logs are stored with encrypted audit trail and retention is configurable. for enterprise Private you can ship logs to your SIEM via forwarders. default retention is 90 days but can be extended. will share SOC2 and logging docs.
[06:45] [07:00] Arjun: going to demo the TypeScript quickstart now. npm init demo, import client, and we call client.generate for embeddings and client.chat for chat. small note: streaming is supported via event stream in TS and Python.
[07:30] Diego: is there an official Node server example for serverless? lambda?
[07:36] Arjun: yep we have an example that uses the event stream and keeps the function warm. link included in repo.
[07:55] Samira: security - we need to understand data residency. our PHI data must stay in region eu-west-1.
[08:05] Lena: you can pin routes to a region. for sensitive data we recommend Redwood Private deployment inside your VPC or Dedicated with region pinning and encryption at rest with your KMS.
[08:30] Tom: latency budget - our SLAs need sub-300ms for short completions. is that achievable?
[08:38] Arjun: depends on model and sequence length. for small models yes; Dedicated gives lower variance. for guaranteed p95s you'll likely want Dedicated + optimized kernels and prefix caching. we can benchmark with your traces.
[08:55] [09:20] Arjun: demoing env var based auth, then switching to service account token flow. code blips, some typing noise.
[10:00] Samira: what about local dev - can devs run without internet or with a sandbox?
[10:08] Arjun: we ship a sandbox image for local dev that mocks the endpoints, and also a lightweight dockerized runner for quick checks. will share the image and how to configure it with .env overrides.
[10:35] Diego: about telemetry - does the SDK send usage stats back? we want opt-out.
[10:42] Lena: by default minimal telemetry (errors, SDK versions) is sent to help with debugging, but it's opt-out via REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=false. in Private you can disable telemetry entirely.
[11:05] Priya: ok we'll need to review the encryption at rest and in flight, plus key management. can you direct us?
[11:12] Maya: yes SOC2 docs and KMS architecture will be in the security pack. i'll put them in the follow up email.
[11:40] [12:00] Arjun: showing sample quickstart test - running a small script to call embeddings on a sample csv. you can see the command: python examples/embeddings.py --input sample.csv --output vectors.json
[12:35] Diego: how do batching and rate limits interplay with our event ingestion? we do large bulk writes at night.
[12:44] Arjun: you can configure batch size and background workers; Redwood Optimize has suggestions and autoscaling policies. for bulk uploads you can use async bulk endpoints or run ingestion against Dedicated where throughput is higher.
[13:10] [14:00] Samira: timeline - we want a pilot in July with real data. what do you recommend for scope?
[14:10] Maya: good, pilot usually is 2-4 weeks: integrate SDK in a single service, run 2 benchmark configs, measure latency and cost, and then evaluate Dedicated if needed. we'll provide an onboarding checklist.
[14:30] Arjun: ok jumping into the console to show API keys and routes - some minor stutter on screen share.
[15:10] Arjun: keys page - you can create keys, name them, and set TTLs. we support rotation via API.
[15:35] Tom: is there infra-as-code for keys and routes?
[15:40] Arjun: yes terraform provider and examples, we'll link the repo.
[16:00] [16:30] Slight crosstalk, someone muted/unmuted.
[17:00] Priya: any third-party attestations? iso?
[17:05] Maya: SOC 2 Type II is available; ISO is in progress. we'll attach the certs.
[17:22] Diego: ok a practical question - our app is in TypeScript microservices, can we easily share typed SDK responses?
[17:30] Lena: yes we have TypeScript types and OpenAPI schemas for routes; the SDK exports types so you get autocomplete.
[18:00] Arjun: now quick look at error handling patterns: retries on 429, circuit breaker examples, and idempotency keys for bulk ingestion.
[18:40] Samira: are function/tool-calling patterns supported? we want to orchestrate model outputs into downstream services.
[18:48] Arjun: yes function calling and structured outputs are supported; examples in the repo.
[19:05] Diego: are there rate limits for the hosted API by default?
[19:12] Maya: we have tiered rate limits; your pilot account can be configured to match expected traffic. Dedicated removes tenant-level throttles.
[19:40] [20:00] Arjun: demoing a short end-to-end: ingest -> embeddings -> vector search -> chat retrieval augmentation. occasional typing/transcription artifacts here.
[22:00] Samira: for the pilot, what's the expected setup work on our side?
[22:10] Maya: main items: create service account or key, wire secrets into CI, add SDK deps to repo, run quickstart example, share sample traces for benchmarking, and schedule 1:1 with Arjun for perf tuning.
[22:35] Diego: ok can you give an example of env config in CI?
[22:40] Arjun: yes e.g. in GitHub Actions: env: REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}; REDWOOD_ENV: prod.
[23:05] Priya: what about the audit trail for who used the keys?
[23:12] Lena: audit logs show key usage with principal and IP; for Private you can forward logs to your Splunk/Datadog.
[23:40] [24:00] Audience asks about SDK versioning and backward compatibility.
[24:10] Arjun: semantic versioning and deprecation schedule documented. major changes announced with migration guides.
[24:40] Samira: cost model - how are we billed per token vs embeddings?
[24:50] Maya: hosted is per-token + embedding unit; Dedicated can be reserved capacity with lower per-token unit economics. we'll share a pricing example for your workload.
[25:20] Diego: could you run a micro-benchmark here? maybe a short inference to show latency numbers?
[25:30] Arjun: sure running a small request against a small model (redwood-1b-quant). result: 120ms median locally (note: transcription may not reflect exact).
[26:00] Priya: do you support customer-supplied models? we have an internal LLM trained on clinical data.
[26:08] Arjun: yes you can bring-your-own-model in Private or Dedicated; we also support model hosting on the Dedicated fleet. integration steps vary but we have an onboarding playbook.
[26:45] [27:30] Maya: circling back to security checklist - Priya please send questions and we'll answer in the security packet.
[27:40] Priya: will do.
[28:00] Diego: ok about error codes - is there a canonical list?
[28:06] Arjun: yes our API docs list error codes and recommended retry semantics.
[28:35] [29:00] Arjun: quick note about SDK telemetry opt-out variable: REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=false.
[29:15] Samira: what's the expected timeline for dedicated/demo resources?
[29:23] Maya: we can provision a pilot sandbox in a few days; Dedicated onboarding takes longer (4-6 weeks) depending on compliance.
[29:45] Diego: do you have real examples of customers in healthcare?
[29:50] Maya: yes we have a few healthtech customers, i'll share sanitized case studies.
[30:15] [31:00] Arjun: now sharing the quickstart links in chat (transcribed as plain text): https://github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts, https://docs.redwood-inference.com/security, https://docs.redwood-inference.com/sdk-quickstart.
[31:40] Priya: for region pinning, is there an override per-route?
[31:46] Lena: yes you can pin a route to eu-west-1 in the console or via infra-as-code.
[32:18] Diego: are there any gotchas with npm package ESM vs CJS?
[32:25] Arjun: we publish both formats and list compatibility notes in README.
[33:05] [34:00] Slight pause, some background noise, then a question on monitoring.
[34:20] Arjun: monitoring: per-route metrics, token-level cost breakdown, and tracing hooks. export to Datadog/Prometheus.
[34:55] Tom: will there be a sandbox Dedicated for us to test PII without touching prod?
[35:02] Maya: yes we can provision a Dedicated-like sandbox for the pilot; it simulates performance and access patterns.
[35:30] Diego: ok last technical item - how do we handle schema evolution for embeddings?
[35:36] Lena: embeddings are versioned and you can tag vector schemas; you'll want to run evals and maintain mapping in your vector store.
[36:10] [37:00] Maya: wrapping up - next steps: we'll send the onboarding checklist + security pack, Arjun will run two benchmarks and share results, and we'll schedule a pilot start meeting.
[37:30] Samira: sounds good, thanks.
[37:40] Diego: thanks everyone.
[37:50] [38:00] End of formal demo, casual chatter about calendars and scheduling.
[40:00] --- brief side conversation scheduling the benchmarking call for 2027-07-02.
[42:00] Priya: i'll send our compliance Qs by Monday.
[43:00] Maya: thanks all, i'll follow up with the links and action items.
[44:30] Call ends.
